definitions.explanation: A container, space, or system that has reached its maximum capacity and cannot hold any more. Used both literally for physical containers and figuratively for schedules, facilities, and similar things.

examples.japanese: ゴミ{箱|ばこ}が{満杯|まんぱい}だ。
{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}はもう{満杯|まんぱい}です。
examples.english: The parking lot is already full.

examples.japanese: {予約|よやく}が{満杯|まんぱい}で、{今月|こんげつ}はもう{空|あ}きがありません。
examples.english: Reservations are completely full, and there are no openings left this month.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective ({満杯|まんぱい}な/{満杯|まんぱい}の) or as a predicate ({満杯|まんぱい}だ). Commonly used for physical containers (trash cans, tanks), facilities (parking lots, hotels), and abstract capacities (schedules, server storage).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {満員|まんいん}: full capacity (specifically for people)
- {満席|まんせき}: all seats taken
- いっぱい: full (more general and conversational)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゴミ{箱|ばこ}が{満杯|まんぱい}: trash can is full
- {駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}が{満杯|まんぱい}: parking lot is full
- {倉庫|そうこ}が{満杯|まんぱい}: warehouse is full
